Chapter 63

Gandhi and His Early Movements

83 facts · 11 Must know

Test mode is on: tap a grey box to reveal the answer.

Key facts from the book (28 points)
  • Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi was born on 2nd October, 1869 AD at Porbandar, Gujarat. Gandhiji's education started in a Pathshala in Porbandar but at the age of seven he moved to Rajkot due to his father's transfer and he studied in Rajkot till high school. Mahatma Gandhi was married to Kasturba Gandhi at the age of 13. He took training as Barrister from ‘Inner Temple’, London. Karamchand Gandhi was Diwan of Porbandar, Wankaner and Rajkot. He is also known as ‘Kaba Gandhi’.
  • Gandhi, in 1894 A.D., founded Natal Indian Congress in South Africa.
  • He along with his colleagues established a new colony named as Tolstoy Farm in 1910 and started living there.
  • He started a newspaper there named Indian Opinion (Published in English, Gujarati, Hindi and Tamil). The first issue of this newspaper was released in June 1903.
  • He established an Ashram at Phoenix (Durban, South Africa) in 1904 A.D. It was reopened on 27th February, 2000 A.D. Phoenix Ashram was the first Ashram established by Gandhiji.
  • In his thoughts Gandhiji emphasized more on practical idealism than idealism. Like Marx he also believed in the removal of State and had no problem on being called as Philosophical Anarchist.
  • Truth and Non-Violence were the two principles of Ram Rajya of Gandhiji. He made these two as the base of Modern society of his dreams. He was a true socialist. He took care of both private and social interests. He wanted to bring functionality to the noble ideals of Social Justice. Gandhiji himself said to Louis Fischer, “I am a true socialist and the aim of my socialism is progress of all”. Socialism of Gandhiji has some glimpses of Marxism. Gandhiji gave extraordinary importance to labours.
  • He wanted to bring into action the principle that everyone is given work according to their capacity and everyone to be paid remuneration according to their needs.
  • Gandhiji said, “I am engaged in solving the same problem that faces scientific socialists. It is true, however that my approach is always and only through unalterated non-violence”. Gandhiji is called an Individualist and Marxist among the socialists.
  • Strike was the last option in the Satyagraha strategy whereas fasting was his first weapon. According to Gandhiji Satyagraha was ‘Agni-Baan’. The objective of Satyagraha of Gandhiji was to change the heart of enemy according to the demand of protestor instead of defeating the enemy. This was to be done by the suffering that Satyagrahi took upon himself. Gandhiji termed self- control as the best solution for Family Planning.
  • Mahatma Gandhi used to say that “Ahimsa and Truth are so intertwined that it is practically impossible to disentangle and separate them. They are like the two sides of a coin, or rather of a smooth unstamped metallic disc. Who can say, which is the obverse, and which is the reverse? Nevertheless, Ahimsa is the means; Truth is the end. Means to be means must always be within our reach, and so Ahimsa is our supreme duty. If we take care of the means, we are bound to reach the end sooner or later. When once we have grasped this point, final victory is beyond question. Whatever difficulties we encounter, whatever apparent reverses we sustain, we may not give up the quest for Truth which alone is, being God Himself”. Mahatma Gandhi was convinced that if we take care of our means, the end will be taken care of itself.
  • In 1893 (24 May), at the age of23, Gandhiji went to Durban (South Africa) to fight a case of Gujarati trader Dada Abdullah. He stayed in Africa for 21 years and returned to India in 1915 A.D. The public welcomed him with enthusiasm, his struggle and victories in South Africa made him popular here too.
  • After coming to India, he met Gopal Krishna Gokhale. He was his political mentor. Gandhiji, for the first time, participated in a Congress session at Calcutta in 1901 A.D. In this session resolution of Gandhiji on Africa was passed. This session was chaired by Dinshaw Wacha. During his stay in South Africa, Gandhiji came to India in 1901 A.D. and established his office of law at Bombay in 1902 A.D. Gandhiji, in 1915 A.D., established Satyagraha Ashram at Ahmedabad. The Ashram was moved to the banks of Sabarmati River on 17th June, 1917 A.D. considering various economic activities.
  • Gandhiji believed that active politics was an important tool for social upliftment and public welfare. In this context the decentralization of power was the most important suggestion of Gandhiji. With the decentralization of power Gandhiji meant the power to Gram Panchayats to manage and administer their villages. The political system shown by Gandhiji was the inclusion of Morality, Religion and Humanity but the complete ideal political system of Gandhiji had no place for State power. He wanted the establishment of stateless society. Gandhiji named the ongoing struggle in Africa as passive resistance, but later on, it was replaced by Satyagraha. It was widely used in India’s struggle for Independence. But both the terms were not the same for Gandhiji. According to him, passive resistance is a political weapon whereas Satyagraha is moral power.
  • During India’s freedom struggle, Gandhiji, in 1917 A.D., started Champaran Satyagraha at Bihar. This was his first successful Satyagraha in India.
  • Gandhiji linked the boycott of foreign clothes with Nation’s Respect. Boycott of foreign clothes by Gandhiji’s Movement was effective as India was believed to be the market for foreign manufactured goods. With Gandhiji’s formula of Boycott offoreign goods the production and sale of Indian goods were promoted.
  • Gandhiji read the book ‘Unto This Last’ written by John Ruskin during his stay in Africa. Gandhiji wrote in his biography that this book changed his life. According to Gandhiji, the Message of this book was - “The good of the individual is contained in the good of all”. On this basis, Gandhiji rendered his ideology of the welfare of all. Among the western thinkers ‘Thoreau, Ruskin and Tolstoy’ highly influenced the Gandhian ideology. From ‘Thoreau’ he learnt civil disobedience and benefits of refusal to pay takes. Ruskin taught him to respect the physical labour. Gandhiji was highly influenced by the statement of Tolstoy- "The Kingdom of God is within you" and this became the base of his non-violence and non-cooperation.
  • Gandhiji worked very hard for the improvement in the conditions of untouchables in India. Gandhiji said, “Service of Harijan is the breath of my life without which I won’t survive one single minute”. Champaran and Kheda were Farmers’ Movement. Champaran movement in Bihar was the first Satyagraha of Gandhiji in India. In the beginning of 19th century white owners of plantations made an obligation with the farmer to cultivate Indigo on 3/20th part of their land. This was called as Teen Kathiya System. Plantation owners imposed Tawan (a lump-sum compensation or illegal levy charges) and other charges/cesses to exploit farmers and make it impossible to get out of the contract. Against this exploitation of the farmers Gandhiji started Champaran Satyagraha. To investigate the matter, the Government constituted a committee and Gandhiji was also one of the members. Plantation owners agreed to return the 25% of illegally collected money. In this way the first Satyagraha of Gandhiji was successful.
  • Pt. Rajkumar Shukla persuaded Gandhiji to look into the matters of the exploitation of farmers in Champaran. The people that accompanied Gandhiji to Champaran for investigation included - Acharya J.B. Kriplani, Dr. Rajendra Prasad, Mahadev Desai, C.F. Andrews, Dr. Anugrah Narayan Sinha, Braj Kishor Prasad, etc. N.G. Ranga opposed Gandhiji’s support to Champaran movement, whereas Rabindranath Tagore gave him the title of 'Mahatma'.
  • After Champaran Movment, the next experiment of Gandhiji was the dispute between cotton mill owners and labours of Ahmedabad on the issue of plague bonus. Gandhiji convinced workers and owners to hand over this issue to a tribunal. To encourage and motivate the labourers, he himself sat on fasting. This protest showed some result and the owners handed over all these matters to the tribunal. Later on tribunal pronounced a 35% increase in dearness allowance (wage increment).
  • In 1918 A.D., at Kheda, after the failure of crops. The Government didn’t give any concession in revenue, nor did they stopped the collection of land revenue. On this matter, Gandhiji constituted a Satyagraha in favour offarmers.
  • Subhash Chandra Bose, for the first time called Gandhiji as the Father of Nation. In July, 1944, speaking on Azad Hind radio, Subhash Chandra Bose addressed Gandhiji and said, “India's last war of independence has begun. Father of Nation we need your blessings and good wishes on this expedition.”
  • Pyarelal Nayyar was the secretary of Gandhiji (since 1942) during Noakhali communal riots. His sister Sushila Nayyar was the personal Doctor of Gandhiji. Pyarelal played an important role in Gandhiji’s Dandi March. Jamnalal Bajaj (Cloth trader, Banker, Congress Social Worker) was a close associate of Mahatama Gandhi. Jamnalal Bajaj was born at Sikar District (Rajasthan). He was adopted by a rich businessman of Wardha. He got in touch with Gandhiji in 1915 A.D. and remained his follower for life. He took part in the Indian National Congress at the age of 30. He renounced the title of Rai Bahadur protesting the policies of British towards India. He was treasurer of Congress and founder of Gandhi Seva Sangh. He took a deep interest in village industry and handloom clothes. He was jailed in 1923 A.D. for taking part in Nagpur Flag Satyagraha and again in 1930 A.D. during Civil Disobedience Movement.
  • Charles Andrews (Dinbandhu Andrews) began teaching at Saint Stephen's College, Delhi. He was deeply attached with Indians and wanted to be an Indian in all forms. He had strong relations with Rabindranath Tagore, Gopal Krishna Gokhale and Mahatma Gandhi.
  • He stayed too at Phoenix Settlements (Ashram) with Gandhiji. Gandhiji, after seeing him completely devoted towards upliftments of poor, gave him the title of Dinbandhu.
  • Andrews was the president of All India Trade Union Congress in 1925 A.D. and 1927 A.D. He accompanied Gandhiji when he went to London to take part in Round Table Conference.
  • Gandhiji was not a member of Congress during India’s Independence. In the year 1934 A.D., he resigned from Congress. Afterwards, he never became a member of Congress officially but his ideologies played a very significant role in the then political scenario.
  • In 1903, Gandhiji founded a law firm in Johannesburg and stayed there till 1910 (before transit to Tolstoy farm). Gandhiji applied the principles of Trusteeship. Gandhiji believed that the economy of each country should be determined after keeping into consideration the climate, land, nature of residents of that country. This economics is totally opposed to exploitation, whether done by one group to the other group of a country or exploitation of a country by another country. Gandhiji wanted to establish such a system in which a person with his fundamental efforts in a free environment can choose to work and perform labour. For this, he wanted the revival of Indian goods industries so that there is enough food to feed all and no one suffers from hunger. Gandhiji emphasized on the importance of cottage industries like - making jaggery, thrashing grass, extracting oil, paper making, leather works etc. with this Gandhiji believed that the poor and exploited will have Social and Economic improvement. On 30th January, 1948, Nathuram Godse shot Gandhiji. On his death, Nehruji said, “The light has gone out of our lives and there is darkness everywhere. I do not know what to tell you and how to say it. Our beloved leader, Bapu as we called him, the Father of The Nation, is no more."

Karamchand (Kaba) Gandhi, Gandhiji's father → Diwan of Porbandar, Rajkot and Wankaner (all three).

Chapter 64

Peasant Movement and Kisan Sabha

23 facts · 6 Must know

Test mode is on: tap a grey box to reveal the answer.

Key facts from the book (13 points)
  • Workers of Home Rule League were very active in Awadh. They started to organize Peasants. Organization was named as 'Kisan Sabha'.
  • U.P. Kisan Sabha was formed in February 1918 A.D. by Indra Narayan Dwivedi, Gauri Shankar Mishra with the support of Madan Mohan Malaviya. The organizations organized peasants on a large scale.
  • These organizations spread awareness amongst the farmers on such a large scale that in 1918 A.D. Delhi Session of Congress a huge number of farmers participated from U.P.
  • In Pratapgarh District of Oudh ‘Nai-Dhobi bandh’ social boycott movement was started against the exploiting landlords.
  • Jhinguri Singh and Durgapal played an important role in this movement, but later on, a new face, Baba Ramchandra emerged who operated the movement wisely and made it strong and combative. In mid 1920 A.D., he emerged as a peasant’s leader and started organizing peasants in Oudh. He had extraordinary organizational capability. In 1920 A.D., with his efforts, Oudh Kisan Sabha was established.
  • Swami Sahajanand Saraswati was the founder of Bihar Provincial Kisan Sabha (BPKS) in 1929. In his Agricultural Reform programme, the main aim was the eradication of Zamindari system and to bring ownership rights to the farmers. For his devoted services to farmers he is also called as ‘Kisan-Pran’.
  • On April 11, 1936. All India Kisan Congress was formed in Lucknow. Swami Sahajanand became its first President and N.G. Ranga became first General Secretary.
  • The Kisan Congress was later renamed as 'All India Kisan Sabha' (AIKS) held its session at the same time of the Congress session in Faizpur which was chaired by N.G. Ranga.
  • Eka Movement (1921-22 A.D.) was led by Madari Pasi of a lower class family. The main centres of this movement were Hardoi, Barabanki, Bahraich and Sitapur. Main complains of farmers included the increment in rent and the system of collection of rent in produce. Rent was 50% higher than the recorded rent generally. In this movement, people didn’t refuse to pay rent and insisted on collecting the revenue in cash because of high inflation.
  • Vallabh Bhai Patel led the peasant movements in 1928 A.D. from Bardoli which later on became popular as Bardoli Satyagraha. With the success of this movement, the women of Bardoli gave the title of ‘Sardar’ to Vallabh Bhai Patel.
  • When the kisan leaders found that large sections of Bargadars were eagerly awaiting a call for struggle for their ‘Tebhaga demand’ and that their mass militancy was at a high pitch, the Bengal Provincial Kisan Council decided, in September 1946, to a launch the ‘Tebhaga Movement’ in the ensuing harvesting season in November 1946. In this movement share-croppers demanded that the share of the Zamindars to be reduced to one-third from the present half of the produce. Rest of the produce i.e. two-third should go to the Share Cropper. The districts of North Bengal and beyond were most affected by this movement.
  • Acharya Vinoba Bhave visited Nalgonda district; Phochampally/Bhudhan Pochampally, is now in Yadadri Bhuvanagiri district (which is carved out of Nalgonda district) of Telangana on 18 April 1951 A.D., in relation to Sarvodaya conference. This district was then the centre of communist activities. Vinoba ji stayed at Bhudan Pochampalli village. Ramchandra Reddy, a landlord of that village donated 100 acres of land to 40 Harijan families to solve their problems of the land.
  • Bhoodan movement began on 18th April 1951, and in October 1951, Vinoba set the target of 50 million acres by 1957; though the movement continued beyond 1957 but later it began to wane.

First peasant movement of India → Bijolia (Mewar, Rajasthan); led by Sadhu Sitaram Das (1913), later Vijay Singh Pathik (1915).

Key facts from the book (10 points)
  • Madras Labour Union was formed in 1918 A.D. under the leadership of B.P. Wadia and V. Kalyanasundaram and it became the First modern labour Union. Buckingham and Carnatic Clothe Mills labourers were part of this union. Soon, two Labour Unions in Bombay, one at Calcutta (The Indian Seamen's Union) and four Labour Unions at Madras were established.
  • The Ahmedabad Textile Labour Association was established on February 25, 1920, by Anasuya Sarabhai (she became president of the association) and Mahatma Gandhi. It emerged following the 1918 Ahmedabad mill strike.
  • All India Trade Union Congress was founded by N.M. Joshi on 31st October, 1920 A.D. at Bombay.
  • Lala Lajpat Rai was the first President of All India Trade Union Congress and Joseph Baptista was the Vice President. Dewan Chaman Lal was its General Secretary (they all were among the founding members) The motive behind its formation was the establishment of International Labour Organization in 1919 A.D. So Indian labourers decided to organize themselves as labour unions. This organization was divided for the first time in 1929 A.D. at Nagpur, Jawaharlal Nehru was president at that time.
  • Communist International was founded in March 1919 A.D. by Vladimir Lenin and Bolshevik Party of Russia.
  • M.N. Roy visited Russia on the invitation of Lenin and joined communist International becoming the first Indian to do so. To stop the growing power and influence of Communist activities, some communist members were arrested on the grounds of a conspiracy held in Kanpur. This case is popularly known as Kanpur Conspiracy.
  • British government in 1924 A.D. started cases against M.N. Roy, Shripad Amrit Dange, Ghulam Hussain, Ramcharan Lal Sharma, Muzaffar Ahmed, Shaukat Usmani, Singaravelu Chettiar, Nalini Gupta, Shamuddin Hassan, M.R.S. Velayndhun, Dr. Manilal, Sampurnanand and Satyabhakta in Kanpur conspiracy. The government charged them with the conspiracy of establishing a revolutionary organisation in India.
  • Revolutionary period of trade union is believed to be 1926- 1939 A.D.. During this M.N. Roy, Muzaffar Ahmed, Shripad A. Dange, Shauqat Usmani etc. were the main leader of the Trade Union Movement.
  • In 1940 AD, M.N. Roy established Radical Democratic Party.
  • Saumendra nath Tagore in 1934 established Revolutionary Communist Party of India.

Chapter 66

Rowlatt Act and Jallianwala Bagh Massacre (1919)

21 facts · 8 Must know

Test mode is on: tap a grey box to reveal the answer.

Key facts from the book (7 points)

Government constituted a committee under the Chairmanship of Justice Sidney Rowlatt, in 1917 A.D. with the objective to investigate and report on the nature and extent of the criminal conspiracies connected with revolutionary movements in India and recommending legislative/legal changes. Based on the recommendations made by this committee, an Act was passed in March 1919 A.D. which empowered to arrest/search/detain persons suspected of sedition/revolutionary activity (including without warrant/trial as per provisions). This Act was also called as an act of No Dalil, No Vakil, No Appeal. Rowlatt Act was passed during the tenure of Lord Chelmsford (1916-1921 A.D.) in 1919 A.D. In his struggle against Rowlatt act, Gandhiji used different stages of movements-Rowlatt Satyagraha-hartals/civil disobedience (1919), non-cooperation and Khilafat movement (began in January 1921).

  • First bold step of Gandhiji in All India politics was the Rowlatt Satyagraha.
  • On 13th, April 1919 A.D., a meeting was called to protest against the arrest of two popular leaders of Punjab, Dr. Saifuddin Kitchlew and Dr. Satyapal. The meeting was organized in Jallianwala Bagh Amritsar on the day of Baisakhi. Brigadier General Reginald Edward Harry Dyer ordered to open fire on unarmed peaceful gathering killing nearly estimates 379 individuals and wounding hundreds more (cited by UK Parliament). After the Massacre at Jallianwala Bagh, Rabindranath Tagore renounced the title of Knighthood granted by the British Government.
  • Shankaran Nair resigned from the Viceroy's Executive Council in protest against the massacre.
  • Hunter Commission was constituted by the Government of India to inquire into the incident of Jallianwala Bagh Massacre. C.H. Sitalwad, Pt. Jagat Narayan and Sultan Ahmad Khan were Indian member in this commission. The commission in its report presented in 1920 didn't find government guilty in this incident. It was said that disorder sometimes becomes revolt. That is why Martial law was compulsory and it is fully justifiable to open fire at that huge gathering. Also, this commission said that incident was just as an error in judgement of Dyer.
  • General Dyer was directed to resign his appointment as Brigade commander in India after this incident but British newspaper presented him as the protector of British Empire and British Lords of assembly praised him as the Lion of British Empire. For his services to Britain, he was given the Sword of Honour. In March 1940 A.D., a Revolutionary from Punjab Udham Singh killed the Lieutenant governor (of Punjab at the time of Massacre) Sir Michael O' Dwyer in London to avenge the Jallianwala Bagh killings. Gandhiji was given the task of writing the draft of the report of Congress Investigation Committee on Jallianwala Bagh Massacre.
  • Montagu termed the Jallianwala Bagh Massacre as Preventive Killing.

Khilafat Movement

12 facts · 4 Must know

Test mode is on: tap a grey box to reveal the answer.

Key facts from the book (8 points)
  • Shaukat Ali, Muhammad Ali, Abul Kalam Azad, Hakim Ajmal Khan, Hasrat Mohani and Dr. Ansari were members of the Khilafat Committee constituted to launch Khilafat Movement. Generally, the credit for the starting of Khilafat Movement is given to Ali Brothers, Shaukat Ali and Muhammad Ali.
  • Sultan of Turkey was considered as the Caliph/Khalifa of the Muslim Empire by the Indian Muslims. In the First World War, Turkey was fighting against the Allied countries. During the First World War, British politicians promised Indian Muslims not to disintegrate Turkey Empire, but as the war ended, the Turkey Empire was dismantled by treaty of severes and came to an end in 1922 (after Treaty of Lausanne, 1922), when The last Ottoman Sultan was deposed and left the capital of constantinople in a British warship.
  • Indian Muslims started hating the British Empire and they started a movement to protect Ottoman Empire of Turkey and protect the Caliphate.
  • Khilafat Movement which was started against the disintegration of Turkey Empire got popularity and pace when it was joined by Gandhiji.
  • Mahatma Gandhi was elected the President of the All India Khilafat Committee, in the All India Khilafat conference held under chairmanship of Fazlul Haq held in Delhi on 23-24 November 1919 A.D. on 24th November.
  • Khilafat Movement accelerated with the congress session of December 1919 at Amritsar. Gandhiji looked this as a Golden opportunity for Hindu-Muslim unity. Thus Gandhiji supported Khilafat Movement to get the support of Indian Muslims in the struggle against the British.
  • During the Khilafat Movement Hakim Ajmal Khan renounced the title of Haziq-ul-Mulk given by British government in the year 1908.
  • Md. Ali Jinnah (then a Nationalist) was against the linking of Khilafat Movement with the Nation’s freedom. He suggested Gandhiji not to bring religion in politics. He was against the Gandhiji’s participation in the Khilafat Movement.

Chapter 68

Non-Cooperation Movement

40 facts · 7 Must know

Test mode is on: tap a grey box to reveal the answer.

Key facts from the book (8 points)
  • Congress held a special session in September 1920 A.D. at Calcutta and passed the resolution of Gandhiji on Non Cooperation. The resolution was opposed by several senior leaders like C.R. Das and Madan Mohan Malviya. In December 1920 A.D. this resolution was widely supported and C.R. Das moved the resolution for Non-Cooperation in the Nagpur session.
  • Gandhiji launched Non-Cooperation movement on 1st August, 1920 A.D. A special session of the Congress was held under the leadership of Lala Lajpat Rai in Calcutta in September, 1920 AD to decide upon the momentous issue of Non Cooperation. Discussions were held on the Khilafat question, the Government’s failure to protect the innocent people of the Punjab and punish the British officers. The leaders decided that the only way to vindicate the national honour was to establish Swaraj through the policy of Non-Cooperation. The resolution of non-cooperation formally adopted in this session. The resolution of the Calcutta Congress was ratified at the regular session held in Nagpur in December, 1920 AD. The movement got widespread success in western India, Bengal and Northern India. During this movement, Motilal Nehru, Lala Lajpat Rai, Sardar Vallabh Bhai Patel, Jawahar Lal Nehru and Rajendra Prasad boycotted court and jumped into the movement. Gandhiji promised Swaraj within one year of the launching of Non-Cooperation Movement ifeffectively carried out, at All India Congress Committee. The plan was prepared for a total boycott of Schools, Colleges, Government titles, Government institutions, Foreign goods, etc. This Movement introduced the people with modern techniques of politics and made them hungry for freedom. Communal Unity and massive participation of Muslims was a significant achievements of this movement.
  • The movement destroyed the fear of British power from the hearts of people.
  • At the time when Gandhiji arrived in India, Britain was at World War I. He supported Britain in the war. Gandhiji was given the title of ‘Kaiser-e-Hind’ for his humanitarian work in South Africa, which he returned during the Non-Cooperation Movement.
  • Jamnalal Bajaj returned the title of Rai Bahadur.
  • Tilak supported the Non-Cooperation movement but his death on the first day of the movement (1st August, 1920 A.D.) made him unable to see the fruits of the movement. Tilak agreed with the policy of non-cooperation with the British (as in June 1920), but Tilak opposed his method of boycott (especially boycott of legislative councils elutions established by the 1919 Montagu- Chelmsford Reforms).
  • Chauri Chaura incident took place on 4th February, 1922. At a place called Chauri Chaura in Gorakhpur district in United Provinces, police openly fired at a group of protestors participating in non-cooperation movement, after this, the angered mob burnt down the police station and killed all 23 policemen (3 civilians were also died). This incident is popularly known as the Chauri Chaura incident. After this incident, Gandhiji withdrew the Non-Cooperation Movement seeing it becoming violent. On 11th and 12th February, 1922 A.D. Congress Working Committee at the Bardoli meeting suspended Non-Cooperation Movement. After the events at Chauri Chaura near Gorakhpur, the Working Committee of the Congress resolves that mass civil disobedience contemplated at Bardoli and elsewhere be suspended and instruct the local Congress Committees forth-with to advise the cultivators to pay the revenue and other dues to the Government and whose payment might have been suspended in anticipation of mass civil disobedience, and instructs them to suspend every other preparatory activity of an offensive nature. The suspension of mass civil disobedience shall be continued till the atmosphere is so nonviolent as to ensure the non-repetition of popular atrocities such as at Gorakhpur or hooliganism such as at Bombay and Madras. On February 24th, 1922 All India Congress Committee organized a meeting in Delhi and a limitation was imposed on all activities that amount to a violation of law. In this session, Dr. Moonje introduced a vote of censure condemning Gandhiji’s decision to call off the movement.
  • Rabindranath Tagore emphasized creative programmes rather than movements and protests by masses. He was against the burning of foreign clothes and wrote a letter to Gandhiji to adopt creative activities instead of mass movements. Rabindranath Tagore called the burning of clothes during the Non-Cooperation as unwise and he said he was unable to obey the same. Kashi Vidyapith of Varanasi in 1921 A.D., Gujarat Vidyapith at Ahmedabad in 1920 AD and Jamia Millia Islamia at Aligarh in 1920 A.D. which was later shifted to Delhi, were established during the Non-cooperation Movement. Madan Mohan Malviya established Banaras Hindu University in 1916 A.D. and was its Vice-Chancellor till 1939 from 1919 A.D.

Don't confuse C.R. Das opposed it at Calcutta but moved it at Nagpur.

Chapter 69

Formation of Swaraj Party (1923)

12 facts · 4 Must know

Test mode is on: tap a grey box to reveal the answer.

Key facts from the book (6 points)
  • Central Legislature (Council of States and the Legislative Assembly) and Provincial Legislative Councils, which were established by the Government of India Act, 1919 were boycotted by the Congress on the directions of Gandhiji and they didn't contest the elections of 1920. An atmosphere of hopelessness was created with the withdrawal of Non Cooperation Movement and the arrest of Gandhiji.
  • C.R. Das and Motilal Nehru formulated a new ideology. They proposed that Congress should fight elections to enter the councils be a part of Government and should enter the Legislative Assemblies and the struggle should be continued by being within the Government. But this plan was rejected by the majority of congressmen. C.R. Das (then President of Congress) resigned from the President's post and organised a party within the Congress in January, 1923 A.D. with Motilal Nehru and named it Swaraj Party. The mandate of this party was to become a part of Councils and hinder their working through agitation.
  • C.R. Das became the President of the Party and Motilal Nehru became its General Secretary. S. Srinivasa Iyengar (founder of the Swaraj Party at Madras) and N.C. Kelkar were the other main leaders of Swaraj Party.
  • The Election of Vithalbhai Patel as the Speaker or President of Legislative Assembly in 1925 A.D. is one of the major achievements of the Swaraj Party.
  • Chittaranjan Das was also known as ‘Desh Bandhu’. The meaning of the term ‘Desh Bandhu’ was ‘Friend of the Country’. Chittaranjan Das studied law in London and became an advocate in India.
  • One of his most important achievements was that he helped in the acquittal of Aurobindo Ghose from the Alipore Bomb Conspiracy Case. He said Swaraj should be for common people not only for some sections of the society. Madan Mohan Malviya was the founder member of Hindu Mahasabha.

Chapter 70

Simon Commission (1927)

18 facts · 3 Must know

Test mode is on: tap a grey box to reveal the answer.

Key facts from the book (10 points)
  • The Government of India Act, 1919 had a provision that a commission would be appointed after ten years to study the progress of the government scheme and suggest new steps.
  • An all White seven-membered Indian Statutory Commission popularly known as the Simon Commission was set up by the British Government under Prime Minister Stanley Baldwin in November, 1927 A.D. The Commission was to recommend to the British Government whether India was ready for further constitutional reforms.
  • This commission was chaired by Sir John Simon and had 7 Members. Since none of its members was Indian, it was opposed and boycotted by the Indian National Congress and a section of the Muslim League, headed by Muhammad Ali Jinnah and this commission was termed as 'White commission' by Indians. The commission arrived in Bombay on 3rd February, 1928 A.D. Chairman of this commission Sir John Simon was a member of Liberal Party whereas Clement Attlee who was the Prime Minister of the United Kingdom during India’s Independence was also a member of this Commission from Labour Party.
  • Indian National Congress in its December 1927 A.D. session held at Madras decided to oppose Simon Commission.
  • On 3rd February 1928 A.D., Simon Commission arrived in India and the countrywide strikes followed. The places approached by Commission witnessed complete strikes and slogan “Simon ! Go Back” was used as a protest in several rallies.
  • Lala Lajpat Rai who was leading a rally in the protest against Simon Commission was severely injured in a Lathi charge by Police and he succumbed to his injuries.
  • Lala Lajpat Rai was a major political leader of Punjab who led the freedom struggle against the British Rule. He is also known as ‘Punjab Kesari’.
  • Nehru Report (1928 A.D.) which had a provision for Dominion Status to India was prepared as an answer to the Simon Commission. It was prepared by an all-party committee headed by Motilal Nehru in which Jawaharlal Nehru was the secretary. This Committee had ten members including two Muslim Members. In this report, Dominion Status for India was demanded instead of complete freedom.
  • Constituencies at places reserved for minorities were suggested instead of separate electorates (joint/mixed electorates). This report also suggested the fundamental rights should be granted to Indians such as right of free expression of opinion; right to assemble peaceably and without arms; right to form associations or unions etc.
  • In 1928 A.D., Subhas Chandra Bose and Jawaharlal Nehru founded Independence for India League to demand Complete Independence instead of Dominion Status.

Simon Commission: appointed November 1927 (Baldwin's Conservative Government) to review 1919 Act; visited India 1928; seven members, no Indian → protests. Must know

Chapter 71

Lahore Session of Congress, Proposal of Complete Independence (1929)

8 facts · 3 Must know

Test mode is on: tap a grey box to reveal the answer.

Key facts from the book (9 points)
  • At Ahmedabad Session (1921 A.D.) of Congress, Maulana Hasrat Mohani defined Swaraj as complete independence from all type of foreign control, demanding Congress to adopt complete independence as its goal.
  • C.R. Das was elected as the President of Congress's Ahmedabad session of 1921 A.D. but the session was presided over by Hakim Ajmal Khan (served as acting President) as C.R. Das was in jail.
  • At Calcutta Session of Congress (1928 A.D.), Congress gave ultimatum to British Government either to accept the recommendations of Nehru Report or face a mass movement.
  • Inability of the government to take any action on the Nehru Report compelled the Congress to announce ‘Purna Swaraj’ as its goal in the historic Lahore Session, 1929 A.D. headed by Jawahar Lal Nehru.
  • On 31st December, 1929 A.D. with the stroke of midnight Congress President Pt. Jawaharlal Nehru hoisted the Indian flag of Independence at the bank of Ravi River. Congress working committee at the sitting of 2nd January, 1930 decided to celebrate 26th January, 1930 A.D. as ‘Purna Swaraj Day (Complete Independence day)’ and to celebrate 26th January, every year as ‘Purna Swadhinta Divas’. In this Session during his presidential address, Nehru said, ‘we have but one goal today that of independence'. Congress on 31st December, 1929 A.D. at Lahore Session announced resolutions which included:

Chapter 72

Civil Disobedience Movement

30 facts · 10 Must know

Test mode is on: tap a grey box to reveal the answer.

Key facts from the book (9 points)
  • At Lahore Session, 1929 A.D. Congress Working Committee was empowered to start Civil Disobedience Movement. In February 1930 Congress Working Committee held its second meeting at Sabarmati Ashram and Mahatma Gandhi was given leadership of this Movement.
  • On 12th March, 1930 A.D. Gandhiji started his famous Dandi March. He, with his chosen companions, departed from Sabarmati to Dandi for the Satyagraha on 12th March. After 24 days of a long journey (reached Dandi on April 5, 1930) Gandhi on 6th April, 1930 A.D. at Dandi, broke Salt Law by picking up a lump of Salt at Dandi. And with this symbolic act, Gandhiji officially started the Civil Disobedience Movement.
  • Subhas Chandra Bose compared this March with the March of Napoleon from Elba to Paris.
  • An English Newspaper editor - Brailsford mockingly said. “Can an Emperor be unseated by boiling sea water in a Kettle?” On this comment, Statesman newspaper replied, “Mr. Gandhi can boil the seawater till they got the Dominion Status”.
  • Civil Disobedience Movement spread to the whole country in Gandhiji leadership. In Tamil Nadu, Gandhian leader C. Rajagopalachari started the salt march from Trichinopoly to Vedaranyam on the Vedaranyam beach of Nagapattinam district to break the salt law.
  • On 5th April, 1930 A.D., Gandhiji reached Dandi village and addressed the foreign reporters as well as Indian reporters and said "I want world sympathy in this battle of Right against might", On 5th May, 1930 A.D., Gandhiji was arrested before a planned raid of congress workers at Dharsana salt works (godown) and was sent to Yerwada Jail. Abbas Tayabji became a leader of the Movement after Gandhiji’s arrest and Sarojini Naidu became the leader of the Movement after Abbas Tayyabji's arrest. Sarojini Naidu led the raid at Dharsana salt godown. This incident was elaborated by American reporter Webb Miller.
  • In the North-West Frontier Province (NWFP), Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan founded an organization called Khudai Khidmatgar. They were also known as Red Shirts. This organization emphasized on the national unity also organized movements against British Colonial policies and demanded improvements in the condition of labours. Muslims of NWFR played an important role in Civil Disobedience Movement under the leadership of Khan Abdul Gaffar Khan. During this movement, Garhwal Rifles under the leadership of Chandra Singh Garhwali in Peshawar refused to fire at unarmed gathering.
  • Tribals of Manipur played an active role in the Civil Disobedience Movement under the leadership of ‘Gaidinliu’ a Naga tribal woman. The movement led by her is called as Jiyatarang Movement (1930s).
  • After the Civil Disobedience Movement, Gandhiji focused on creative programmes. On 17th September, 1934 Mahatma Gandhi issued a public statement announcing his resignation from Congress. In October 1934 A.D., Gandhiji officially retired from active politics to devote all his time in the upliftment of Harijans. In September 1932 A.D., Gandhiji founded an All India Anti-Untouchability League and in 1933 A.D. he started a weekly newspaper named Harijan for the betterment of Harijans.

Lahore Session (1929) authorised Congress Working Committee to launch Civil Disobedience; Gandhi named leader at CWC meeting, Sabarmati Ashram, February 1930.

Chapter 73

Gandhi-Irwin Pact

5 facts · 3 Must know

Test mode is on: tap a grey box to reveal the answer.

Key facts from the book (7 points)
  • Viceroy Irwin released Gandhiji from jail on 26th January 1931 AD considering the increasing influence of the Civil Disobedience Movement. Talks between Gandhiji and Irwin started in February 1931 AD with the efforts of Tej Bahadur Sapru and M.R. Jaykar. Gandhi-Irwin Pact was signed on 5th March, 1931. Sarojini Naidu termed Irwin and Gandhiji as ‘Two Mahatmas’. According to this pact -

(1) Under the leadership of Gandhiji, Congress decided to withdraw the Civil Disobedience Movement,

(2) All political prisoners who had not convicted of violence were to be released,

(3) Right to peaceful protest at shops offoreign cloth and liquor shops,

(4) Permission to make salt in the Coastal States without Salt Tax,

(5) Congress agreed to participate in the Second Round Table Conference.

People were disappointed by this pact because it did not include the commulation of the death sentences of Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev and Rajguru. Biographer of Irwin, Alan Campbell Johnson termed the benefits to Gandhi in Gandhi-Irwin Pact as consolation prizes and said this pact was the only surrender of Irwin agreeing to enter into negotiations.

Chapter 75

Round Table Conference

14 facts · 7 Must know

Test mode is on: tap a grey box to reveal the answer.

Key facts from the book (7 points)
  • Simon Commission’s, two volume report was published on 10th June and 24th June, 1930. Political associations rejected this report. Main leaders of Congress were in Jail. British Government organized the first Round Table Conference in London from November 1930 to January 1931 in an atmosphere of dissatisfaction and discouragement. 89 Indian delegates participated but Congress was absent from this conference.
  • Tej Bahadur Sapru, Srinivas Shastri, Md. Ali Jauhar, Md. Shafi, Aga Khan III, Fazlul Haq, Md. Ali Jinnah, Homi Mody, M.R. Jaykar, Dr. B.S. Moonje, B.R. Ambedkar and Sundar Singh Majithia, etc. were the ones who participated in the first Round Table Conference.
  • K.T. Paul represented the Christians in this conference. The conference was inaugurated by His Majesty the King Emperor (George V) and was chaired by British Prime Minister Ramsay MacDonald.
  • Mahatma Gandhi was the sole representative of Congress in the Second Round Table Conference held between 7th September 1931 and 1st December 1931. This conference was joined by leaders like Sarojini Naidu, Madan Mohan Malviya and Annie Besant. Gandhiji travelled to London on S.S. Rajputana ship and stayed at Kingsley Hall in London. The Second Round Table Conference ended on 1st December and Gandhiji returned without any gains. After returning, Gandhiji said, “It is true that I returned barehanded but I am content that the Flag I had been handed was never let down by me and I never compromised with the honour of that flag”.
  • The Second Round Table Conference was totally unsuccessful due to communal issues. B.R. Ambedkar was demanding a separate electorate for Dalits which was not acceptable to Gandhiji.
  • B.R. Ambedkar was the only Indian to take part in all three Round Table Conferences.
  • The Third Round Table Conference was held between 17th November 1932 A.D. to 24th December, 1932 A.D. and Congress boycotted this too.

Chapter 76

Communal Award and Poona Pact (1932)

15 facts · 7 Must know

Test mode is on: tap a grey box to reveal the answer.

Key facts from the book (7 points)
  • A consensus among several parties for the separate electorate for Dalits was not reached in Second Round Table Conference. The His Majesty Government's declared position (endorsed by Parliament) that ifcommunities failed to agree the government would devise and apply a scheme. As a result British P.M. Ramsay MacDonald find a solution (although Europeans, Anglo-Indians, Indian Christians got separate electorates in 1919).
  • On 16th August 1932 A.D. Ramsay MacDonald announced Communal Award. In this award, each minority group was given some reserved seats in Legislative Assemblies and elections to those seats were to be held by a separate electorate. Members of the depressed classes qualified to vote, will vote in a general constituency and they one also entitled to vote in a general constituency.
  • Earlier Muslims and Sikhs were considered minorities but with this award the Dalit section of Hindu constituencies also got separated from it and now considered as a minority. Now Muslims, Indian Christians, Sikhs, Anglo-Indians and others including depressed classes were given separate electorates which were available in elections at Provincial Legislatures only.
  • Gandhiji started his first fast unto death on 20th September, 1932 A.D. from Yerwada jail against the Communal Award which ended with the Poona Pact between B.R. Ambedkar and Gandhiji. Gandhiji didn’t sign this Pact. On 24th September, 1932 A.D. Poona Pact was signed between Dr. Ambedkar from Dalit section and Madan Mohan Malaviya from Hindu community.
  • M.R. Jayakar, Devdas Gandhi, P. Baloo, Gavai, Thakkar, Solanki, T.B. Sapru, G.D. Birla, Rajagopalachari, Dr. Rajendra Prasad, Rao Bahadur Srinivas, M.C. Rajah, C.V. Mehta, Bakhale and Kamat signed this Pact too.
  • 71 seats were reserved for Depressed classes in Communal Award which was increased to 148 by Poona Pact (Madras-30, Sindh with Bombay - 15, Punjab - 8, Bihar and Orissa - 18, Central Provinces - 20, Assam - 7, Bengal -30 and United Provinces 20). (This number is however 147 in some books). Also, 18% of General seats were reserved for the Dalits in central legislature. After the Poona Pact, Gandhiji didn't show more interest in the Civil Disobedience Movement and shifted his focus towards the fight against untouchability. He founded All India Anti-Untouchability League which was later renamed ‘Harijan Sevak Sangh’. Ghanshyam Das Birla was its first President.

All India Depressed Classes League was founded by Babu Jagjivan Ram. All India Scheduled Castes Federation was founded by B.R. Ambedkar in 1942 A.D., while All India Depressed Classes Association was founded in 1926 A.D. by M.C. Rajah. On 14th August, 1931 A.D., B.R. Ambedkar in a conversation with Gandhiji said that "History tells that Mahatmas, like fleeting phantoms, raise dust, but raise no level".

Chapter 77

Congress Socialist Party (1934)

9 facts · 4 Must know

Test mode is on: tap a grey box to reveal the answer.

Key facts from the book (5 points)
  • In May 1934, the All India Congress Committee met at Patna to set up a Congress Parliamentary Board to fight elections under the aegis of Congress itself. However, some of the members of All India Congress Committee held separate meetings and founded All India Congress Socialist Party, and this party was officially inaugurated in October 1934 A.D. The policies and working methods were to be decided in a meeting that was to be held in Bombay.
  • Jaya Prakash Narayan was the convener of All India Congress Socialist Party in Patna, 1934. He was the general secretary of party and Acharya Narendra Dev was the President. The objective of the was to push the Indian National Congress towards a clear socialist agenda, focusing on full independence, abolition of landlordism and nationalisation of key industries. Its members were :- Ashok Mehta, Achyut Patwardhan, Minoo Masani, Dr. Ram Manohar Lohia, Purushottam Trikam Das, Yusuf Meherally, Ganga Sharan Sinha and Kamla Devi Chattopadhyay, etc. Bihar Socialist Party was founded by Ganga Sharan Sinha, Rambriksha Benipuri and Ramanand Mishra (in 1991). Sri Narsingh Narayan Azad was a socialist and was an important member of Bihar Socialist Party.
  • J.P. Narayan belonged to Bihar Socialist Party.
  • J.P. Narayan also known as Loknayak secretly organized Indian masses during Quit India movement with the help of Dr. Ram Manohar Lohia and Aruna Asaf Ali. On 5th June, 1974, he called for total revolution (Sampoorna Kranti) from Gandhi Maidan. He was awarded Bharat Ratna posthumously in 1999. In April, 1946 A.D., ‘Jaya Prakash Day’ was celebrated for the release of Jaya Prakash from prison. A rally was conducted in Bankipur Maidan of Patna where the release of Jaya Prakash Narayan was demanded and criticism of government policy regarding the arrest of political persons was made.
  • In May, 1936 A.D., 21 businessmen of Bombay signed Bombay Manifesto. The manifesto was against propagating the principles of socialism as conveyed by Nehru in Lucknow Session.

Chapter 78

Provincial Election and Formation of Cabinet (1937)

10 facts · 4 Must know

Test mode is on: tap a grey box to reveal the answer.

Key facts from the book (13 points)
  • On the basis of Government of India Act, 1935, in February 1937, election results were announced of provincial legislatures in which Congress by defeating its opponents secured majority in five provinces.

1. Madras (159 seats out of total 215 seats) - Congress

2. Bihar (98 seats out of total 152 seats) - Congress

3. Central Provinces and Berar (70 out of 112) - Congress

4. United Provinces (134 seats out of 228) - Congress

5. Orissa (36 out of 60 seats) - Congress

  • Congress emerged as the single largest party in Bombay (86 seats out of 175), Assam and North-West Frontier Province. Only in Bengal, Punjab and Sindh did Congress not secure enough support from masses to form the government on its own. The cabinets formed by Congress after 1936-37 A.D. elections only lasted for 28 months. In July 1937 A.D., Congress formed cabinets in 6 provinces - Madras, Bombay, Central Province, Orissa, Bihar, and United Province and with the support of other parties Congress formed a coalition government in Assam (a coalition government was formed by Muhammad Saadulla in 1937, but later resigned and Congress government led by Gopinath Bordoloi took office in September 1938) and North-West Frontier Provinces. Based on 1937 results, Sir Sahibzada Abdul Qayyum Khan, formed a coalition government although Indian National Congress was the single largest party, the Congress formed the government there by moving no-confidence motion against Qayyum Khan. The inclusion of Indians into the Second World War without consultation led to the resignation of all Congress cabinets. On 22nd October, 1939 A.D. Congress cabinet of all provinces resigned as an act of protest. Congress coalition government in Assam under Gopinath Bordoloi was resigned from the government in November, 1939 and the NWFP government was also resigned in November, 1939. On the resignation of the Congress cabinets, Jinnah called Indian Muslims to celebrate 22nd December, 1939 A.D. as a Day of Deliverance.
  • Working Committee of Indian National Congress decided for abolition of feudal intermediaries/peasants proprietorship in 1937 A.D. as a result of which Congress governments in U.P. and Bihar passed tenancy bills. Congress secured 134 seats out of 228 seats in United Provinces and formed government on its own.
  • Govind Ballabh Pant was the Prime Minister (Premier) while Kailash Nath Katju was Law and Justice Minister and Revenue/Home/ Jail Ministry was given to Rafi Ahmed Kidwai.

Chapter 84

Cripps Mission (1942)

7 facts · 1 Must know

Test mode is on: tap a grey box to reveal the answer.

Key facts from the book (7 points)

Considering the rising power of Japan, international community, especially United States of America, China and Australia pressured Britain for political solution settlement with India. Due to urgent need for British action to solve the political problem, Stafford Cripps arrived in India in March, 1942 A.D. to negotiate with Indian politicians.

After reaching India in March, 1942 A.D., Stafford Cripps presented a proposal whose major recommendations were:

i- After Second World War India should be given a Dominion Status which is consistent with the declaration (i.e. associated by common allegiance to the crown, while not subordinate in domestic/external affairs).

ii- Indians should be given the right to form their own Constitution for which the elected constitution making body will be initiated after the War.

iii- Any provinces not agreeing to the new Constitution would have the right to keep themselves out of the proposed Union. and to retain its present constitutional position.

  • Mahatma Gandhi termed this deal as a post-dated cheque on a falling bank.
  • Pt. Jawaharlal Nehru and Maulana Azad were the official negotiators from the Congress side in talks with Cripps Mission.

Cripps Mission → Stafford Cripps arrived March 1942; pressure from USA, China, Australia amid rising power of Japan.

Chapter 85

Quit India Movement

45 facts · 10 Must know

Test mode is on: tap a grey box to reveal the answer.

Key facts from the book (34 points)
  • During 5-14 July, 1942 A.D., a meeting of Congress Committee was held at Wardha. It was attended by prominent leaders of Congress like Jawahar Lal Nehru, Abul Kalam Azad, Vallabh Bhai Patel, Mahatma Gandhi, Aruna Asaf Ali, Achyut Patwardhan, Dr. Anugrah Narayan Sinha, Pattabhi Sitaramayya etc.
  • ‘Quit India’ resolution was passed in this meeting on July 14, 1942. It was chaired by then Congress President Abul Kalam Azad.
  • On 7th -8th August, 1942 A.D., meeting of All India Congress Committee was held at Gowalia Tank (now August Kranti ground) in Bombay. Wardha Resolution was confirmed in this meeting.
  • After a few modifications, the resolution for Quit India movement was passed on 8th August, 1942 A.D. Quit India Movement for India’s Independence was launched on 9th August 1942. Gandhiji gave a statement before the official launch of Quit India Movement. The statement had the following important points.

1) Government officials should announce their support and devotion to Congress.

2) Soldiers should refuse to fire on their countrymen.

3) Students should quit studies only ifthey stood firmly on this decision until independence.

4) Kings should accept the sovereignty of their people and declare their province as a part of the Indian nation. Masses should accept the leadership of the king only if he sees his future in the future of Masses.

  • In his speech Gandhiji said :- "I am not going to be satisfied with anything short than complete freedom". It may be possible that Salt Tax and drink evil, etc. may be abolished or stopped by the English Government but my words will demand 'Nothing less than complete Freedom'. Today I give you a mantra “Do or Die”. This mantra means that either we will free our country or will die fighting for Independence.
  • On 8th August, 1942 A.D., Jawahar Lal Nehru presented the ‘Quit India resolution’ to All India Congress Committee. This proposal was supported by Sardar Vallabh Bhai Patel. The draft of this proposal was prepared by Mahatma Gandhi himself with the help of Jawahar Lal.
  • Hindu Mahasabha, Communist Party of India, Unionist Party (Punjab) and Muslim League were not in favour of this movement. On 9th August, 1942 A.D., Quit India Movement was launched. In the early hours of the Movement, Gandhiji and other important leaders of Congress were arrested under Operation Zero Hour.
  • Gandhiji, Sarojini Naidu and other leaders were arrested and taken to Aga Khan Palace.
  • Members of Congress working Committee (Jawaharlal Nehru, Abul Kalam Azad, Govind Ballabh Pant, Dr. Prafful Chandra Ghosh, Dr. Pattabhi Sitaramayya, Dr. Syed Mahmud, Acharya Kriplani) were arrested and taken to Ahmednagar Fort.
  • Dr. Rajendra Prasad, member of Congress Working Committee couldn't come to Bombay, he was arrested and kept at Patna (Bankipur) Jail. Shivkumar and Ram-nandan Mishra (he was first arrested in Cuttack but later he was transferred to Hzaribagh). were arrested in Hazaribagh.
  • Movement of 1942 showed maximum impact in Bombay, Bengal, Bihar, Orissa, United Province of Agra and Oudh and Madras but the participation of the whole country was necessary for this movement to succeed.
  • Lord Wavell was the commander in chief of India during Quit India Movement (1942 A.D.). He served as Viceroy from the year 1943 A.D. to 1947 A.D.
  • Winston Churchill was the Prime Minister of England during Quit India Movement.
  • Abul Kalam Azad was the President of Congress when the resolution of Quit India Movement was passed. He was elected President in Ramgarh Session of Congress in 1940 A.D. and after that for five years (1941-45 A.D.) no session of Congress was held and Abul Kalam Azad continued to be the President of Congress for these years. He was the President of Congress for the maximum years before independence, also the political scenario of India was very fragile during his tenure.
  • During Quit India Movement, a secret radio station of Congress was broadcasted from different parts of Bombay Dr. Ram Manohar Lohia played a significant role in the Quit India Movement. He directed the movement while remaining underground. He also established an undergraound radio station.
  • Usha Mehta was an important member of the group of Congress that broadcasted radio being underground.
  • Louis Fischer, an Americanjournalist, was with Gandhiji just before Quit India Movement as he came to India in May 1942 and spent one week with Gandhiji at Sevagram Ashram, Wardha. (He was biographer of Gandhiji).
  • Louis Fischer, with American intellectuals Pearl Buck, Edgar Snow, Fredrick L. Schuman and Norman Thomas demanded India’s Independence.
  • Riots emerging out of Quit India Movement were widespread in Bihar and United Provinces It emerged as a revolt. Eastern United Provinces (including Azamgarh, Ballia, Gorakhpur) and Gaya, Champaran, Saran, Purnia, Shahabad, Muzaffarpur, and Bhagalpur areas of Bihar were self instilled centres of mass revolt.
  • August Movement of 1942 A.D. became widespread among the farmers. Some groups of farmers performed agricultural activities in the day and took part in rioting activities at night. Their fierceness and strength demonstrated the glimpses of the revolt of1857, that is why Viceroy Linlithgow in a telegram to British Prime Minister Winston Churchill termed this movement as by far the most serious rebellion after the Revolt of 1857.
  • During the Quit India Movement, Jayaprakash Narayan fled from Hazaribagh jail and became active in the underground activities. Yogendra Shukla too fled with J.P. Narayan on 9th November, 1942 A.D. but was later arrested in Muzaffarpur and sent to Patna.
  • On the speech given by Gandhiji during Quit India Movement (1942 A.D.), Pattabhi Sitaramayya said, “In reality that day Gandhiji was speaking after being motivated with the power of Avatar and Paigambar.
  • Rashtriya Swayam Sevak Sangh didn’t participate in Quit India Movement. It didn’t participate in any movement between 1940 A.D. and 1947 A.D. till foreign rule ended.
  • Aruna Asaf Ali was a famous freedom fighter. She will always be remembered for hoisting the tricolour Flag at Gowalia Tank ground (Bombay) during Quit India Movement.
  • ArunaAsafAli, Usha Mehta, J.P. Narayan, Ram Manohar Lohia, etc being underground provided alternate leadership to the Quit India Movement when all other prominent leaders were arrested.
  • Establishment of Parallel Government at several places was an important feature of Quit India Movement. These were:-

1. Ballia - August 1942 A.D. - Chittu Pandey led the Government.

2. Tamluk (Midnapore) Bengal - From December 1942 to August 1944 AD the Tamralipta Jatiya Sarkar in Tamluk started the relief programmes for the persons affected by storms.

3. Satara (Maharashtra) - A Parallel Government named Prati Sarkar was formed in August-1943 A.D. It was the longest-serving Parallel Government till May 1946 A.D. Its main leaders were - Y.B. Chavan and Nana Patil. There was a Parallel Government in Talchar, Orissa too for some time.

  • Gandhiji was released on 6th May, 1944 A.D. on account of bad health conditions. On Gandhiji's release, Winston Churchill remarked, “When we are winning around the globe how can we be defeated by this old man who is our enemy for a long time.”

Chapter 86

Subhas Chandra Bose and Azad Hind Fauj

33 facts · 9 Must know

Test mode is on: tap a grey box to reveal the answer.

Key facts from the book (15 points)
  • Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose was born on 23rd January, 1897 A.D. at Cuttack, Orissa (Odisha) division of Bengal province. He graduated from Scottish Church College (Affiliated to University of Calcutta) in 1919 A.D. and passed the Indian Civil Services exam in 1920 A.D. He became president of Congress in the session of 1938 A.D. and 1939 A.D. In 1939 AD, he resigned from Congress presidentship and founded Forward Bloc. He went to Germany in the year 1941 A.D. He gained control of Azad Hind Fauz in the sessions of 1943 A.D. He is often remembered as Netaji.
  • Gurudev Rabindra Nath Tagore gave him the title of Desh Nayak.
  • Mahatma Gandhi called him as Patriot of Patriots.
  • In Germany, with the help of German Government he founded “Free India Centre” where he printed several pamphlets for India's Independence and gave many speeches. Starting from In the year 1941 A.D., Subhas Chandra Bose recruited thousands of Indian war prisoners from General Erwin Rommel of North Africa, and formed an army of thousands of soldiers (war prisoners), this was called as “The Free Indian Legion”. The provisional government of free India (Arzi-Hukumat-e-Azad Hind) was formally proclaimed by Subhas Chandra Bose in October 1943 in Singapore.
  • Azad Hind Fauz was basically founded by Capt. Mohan Singh who was British Indian Army Officer. When the British Army was retreating in the war with Japan, Mohan Singh joined hand with Japanese. After this Japanese gave Indian soldiers to Mohan Singh and he started recruiting them in Azad Hind Fauz.
  • In December 1941, in Malay Forests, the Punjab battalion led by Mohan Singh was defeated by the Japanese army. Lt. Colonel L.V. Fitz Patrick (English Origin) was the prisoner of war but Bangkok resident Indian Giani Pritam Singh took their responsibility and became successful in establishing friendship between the Japanese and Mohan Singh with other Indian soldiers.
  • Japanese Major Iwaichi Fujiwara and Giani Pritam Singh encouraged Capt. Mohan Singh to lead Indian National Army. In December 1941, Capt. Mohan Singh agreed to it and in February 1942 under his leadership Indian National Army was founded in which the defeated Indian soldiers of the British Army who went on Malay expedition were recruited. It should be made clear here that the brainchild of INA was given by Mohan Singh, Giani Pritam Singh and Iwaichi Fujiwara.
  • Mohan Singh did the brave task of providing leadership to it.
  • Azad Hind Fauz (I.N.A.) was constituted officially in September, 1942 and Captain Mohan Singh became its first Commander. On 4th July, 1943 A.D., Rash Behari Bose gave the command of I.N.A. to Subhas Chandra Bose.
  • On 21st October 1943 A.D., Subhas Chandra Bose established a Provisional Government of Free India (Azad Hind Sarkar) at Singapore. On August 26, 1943, Bose officially took charge of INA and renamed it as Azad Hind Fauj. Fauz was founded on the Singapore. Singapore was under Japanese occupation (1942-1945). Singapore became a part of Malaysia in 1963 A.D.
  • On 9th August, 1965 A.D., Malaysia Parliament with a Agreement separated Singapore from State of Malaysia. On this day, Singapore became a free country. So, it is clear that Singapore was part of Malaya when Azad Hind Fauz was formed.
  • In Burma (Myanmar), Netaji appealed to his soldiers and said, “we have sacrificed a lot but the ultimate sacrifice of our life is remaining, we need the priests who is ready to sacrifice his life to the Goddess of freedom for the Independence of his country, Give me Blood, I promise you Freedom”. The slogan 'Jai Hind' was suggested by Abid Hasan, Base's secretory, this slogan was formally adopted as the greeting in Azad Hind Fauj. It was the tradition of Salute in Azad Hind Fauz, today it is the slogan of the whole nation.
  • Azad Hind Fauz Day was celebrated on 12th November, 1945 A.D. and they celebrated from 5th November to 11th November, 1945 A.D. Azad Hind Fauz week. Soldiers and officers of Azad Hind Fauz were arrested and court martial proceedings against them were filed by the British Government in November 1945 AD at Delhi Red Fort. As a result of which three convicts Prem Sahgal, Gurbaksh Singh Dhillon and Shah Nawaz were sentenced to transportation for life and Abdul Rashid was awarded 7 years of imprisonment.
  • Congress constituted an INA Defence Committee, to rescue them in which prominent advocates were - Bhulabhai Desai (leader of the Committee), Tej Bahadur Sapru, Kailash Nath Katju, Asaf Ali and Jawahar Lal Nehru. There were countrywide protests against the sentence of the court, which compelled then Commander-in-ChiefClaudeAuchinleck to commute the transportation for life sentences of three defendant and to free other soldiers of INA also.
  • Jawahar Lal Nehru succeeded in passing a resolution of Guerrilla warfare against the Japanese in the Congress Working Committee at Allahabad (Prayagraj). He was opposed to Nazism, Fascism and Imperial Ideologies.

Subhas Chandra Bose: born 23 January 1897, Cuttack (Odisha); ICS 1920; Congress President 1938 and 1939; founded Forward Bloc 1939; fled to Germany 1941.

Chapter 87

Cabinet Mission Plan (1946)

12 facts · 4 Must know

Test mode is on: tap a grey box to reveal the answer.

Key facts from the book (8 points)
  • Clement Attlee became British Prime Minister on 26th July, 1945 A.D. British Prime Minister Clement Attlee announced on February 19th, 1946 A.D., the dispatch of the Cabinet Mission for constitutional reforms. Cabinet Mission arrived in Delhi on 24th March 1946 A.D. The Cabinet Mission to India consisted Lord Pethick Lawrence was secretory of State for India Sir Stafford Cripps the President of the Board of Trade and A.V. Alexander, First Lord of the Admiralty. They arrived on March 24, 1946 A.D. and held extensive discussions in April with almost all major leaders of the country. The Cabinet Mission proposed a three-tier polity for India. The major recommendation of the Cabinet Mission was to divide the provinces into three sections i.e. A, B and C.
  • On 16th May, 1946 A.D. Cabinet Mission announced its recommendations and its main proposals were-

(1) There should be a Union of India, embracing both British India and the states, which should deal with the following subjects – foreign affairs, defence and communications; of India would be given Independence.

(2) The Muslim League’s demand for Pakistan was rejected.

(3) The Union should have an Executive and Legislature constituted from British India Province and Princely State Representatives.

(4) A Constituent Assembly would be formed with the representatives of Provincial Legislative Assembly Chief Commissioners Provinces and the Princely States.

  • Cabinet Mission also recommended reorganization of Viceroy’s Executive Council and formation of the interim government in which all the ministerial posts including war member would be held by Indians.
  • Gandhiji supported Cabinet Mission and said this proposal is the best document the British Government could have produced in the circumstances, while cautioning that their best may possible be harmful. Maulana Abul Kalam Azad was the Congress President during the arrival of Cabinet Mission.

Chapter 88

Constituent Assembly (1946)

10 facts · 2 Must know

Test mode is on: tap a grey box to reveal the answer.

Key facts from the book (10 points)
  • The early non-official draft of Constituent Assembly was enshrined in Swaraj Bill of 1895, which was influenced by Bal Gangadhar Tilak’s directions. In the 20th century, Gandhiji firstly pointed towards this idea when in the year 1922 AD he said that the Indian Constitution should be made as per India’s need. On February 8, 1924, Motilal Nehru officially introduced a resolution in the Central Legislative Assembly, known as the 'National Demand' calling for a round table conference to establish a constitution-making body, marking a pivotal early demand for a Constituent Assembly. After this M.N. Roy proposed this demand and the basic concepts of Constituent Assembly was reiterated by Jawahar Lal Nehru. Congress in Faizpur Session (December 1936 AD) reaffirmed the idea of the Constituent Assembly and also pointed out its importance. Constituent Assembly was formed on the recommendation of the Cabinet Mission Plan.
  • On 24 March, 1946 AD, Cabinet Mission arrived at Delhi. During the announcement of this mission, its Secretary of State for India, Pethick Lawrence made it clear that the aim of this mission was to prepare a plan for the formation of Constituent Assembly to make a constitution of free India and to make proper arrangements of an interim government for the Indians.
  • As per the Cabinet Mission plan, for the formation of Constituent Assembly each provinces were given the number of seats in the proportion of one seat for every Ten lakh of the population. Three voter groups were made - General, Muslims and Sikhs (Only in Punjab).
  • Elections for the 296 seats of the Constituent Assembly were held in provinces in July 1946 AD.
  • In the constituent Assembly, 208 Congress members were elected, 73 Muslim League candidates were winners and 15 others were elected.
  • Md. Ali Jinnah was not a member of Constituent Assembly of India. The first meeting of Constituent Assembly was held on 9 December, 1946 AD. Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha was its first provisional (temporary) Chairman.
  • On 11th December, 1946 AD, its meeting was held at Delhi and Dr. Rajendra Prasad was elected as its Permanent Chairman.
  • Indian Constitution was adopted on 26th November, 1949 AD. At the time of its formation, the Constituent Assembly was not a sovereign institution.
  • On the midnight of 14th August, 1947 AD, Constituent Assembly was declared as a sovereign body of the Dominion of India with Dr. Rajendra Prasad as its President.
  • G.V. Mavalankar held the posts of Speaker of Central Legislative Assembly and the speaker of House of the People (Lok Sabha). He was the speaker of Central Legislative Assembly from 24 January 1946 AD to 14th August, 1947 AD and became the first speaker of Lok Sabha after India’s Independence. He was the Speaker of Lok Sabha from 1952 to 1956. He was the Speaker of Bombay Legislative Assembly from the year 1937 AD to 1946 AD.

Don't confuse Option 'Swaraj Party in 1935' has the wrong year; Swaraj Party's Ranchi demand was 1934.

Key facts from the book (9 points)
  • On 12th August, 1946 AD Lord Wavell invited Congress President Jawahar Lal Nehru to form the Interim Government. On 24th August, 1946 AD under the leadership of Jawaharlal Nehru, Congress announced a communique offirst Interim Government of India. On 2nd September, 1946 AD First Interim Government of India was formed in which Muslim League didn’t participate in the beginning.
  • Dr. Rajendra Prasad was the Minister of Agriculture and Food in the Interim Government. Baldev Singh was Defence Minister. External affairs and Commonwealth Affairs were looked after by Jawahar Lal Nehru in this interim government. Asaf Ali held Communication (Rail and Transport) Ministry in the interim government of 1946 AD.

Rajagopalachari, Sharat Chandra Bose, Dr. John Mathai, Sardar Baldev Singh, Sir Shafat Ahmed Khan, Jagjivan Ram, Syed Ali Zaheer and C.H. Bhabha. The All India Muslim League formally demanded a separate state for muslims, known as the Pakistan Resolution (or Lahore Resolution) on March 23, 1940 as its general session in Lahore. The League officially decided to join the interim Government on October 13, 1946 (after the direct action day). Initially they boycotted the government established on September 2, 1946.

Chapter 90

Partition of India and Independence

39 facts · 10 Must know

Test mode is on: tap a grey box to reveal the answer.

Key facts from the book (18 points)
  • Clement R. Attlee was the Prime Minister of Britain when India got Independence from Britishers. He was the Prime Minister from the year 1945 to 1951 AD. Clement Attlee was from the Labour Party. On 20th February, 1947 AD, Attlee in House of Commons declared that by a date before June, 1948 AD we will free India and transfer the power of the Government in Indian hands.
  • Attlee made Lord Mountbatten the viceroy after replacing Wavell. Mountbatten came to India in March 1947 AD, and started the proceedings of transfer of power. He was given the task of the transfer of power in the manner that will best ensure the future happiness and prosperity of India and take decisions as per the need of India so that Britain could depart from India with honour and with minimal damage.
  • Mountbatten during the talks on the transfer of power reached a conclusion that partition of India and formation of Pakistan is a must. He prepared a plan, keeping in mind the instructions by Attlee. The plan was prepared for the partition of India, this plan is known as the Mountbatten Plan (3rd June, 1947 AD).
  • As per the plan on July 1947 AD, Indian Independence Act was passed by the British Parliament in which two nations India and Pakistan were given dominion status and the deadline for the formation of Pakistan and India as two nations were fixed to 15th August, 1947 AD.
  • Indian Independence Bill was presented by Attlee on 4th July, 1947 AD in the House of Commons in British Parliament. House of Commons passed this Bill on 15th July, 1947 AD and was passed by House of Lords the next day. The Bill got Royal Assent of his Majesty on 18th July, 1947 AD.
  • Between 24 March and 6 May 1947 AD, in series of 133 full records of talks with Indian politicians Mountbatten reached on a conclusion that Cabinet Mission Plan had been impractical. So he prepared another substitute plan for this and termed it as “Plan Balkan”.
  • Punjab Boundary Commission and Bengal Boundary Commission were formed by Mountbatten on 30th June, 1947 AD to determine the division of land between India and Pakistan along with Punjab and Bengal. Cyril Radcliffe was the chairman of both the Councils. The councils was given the task to demarcate the boundaries of Punjab and Bengal on the basis of Contiguous majority areas of Muslim and Non Muslim majority population. For this task, he had to take in consideration of various other elements too. Each council had four members (judges) two from Congress and two from the Muslim League. Gandhiji, in his first meeting with Mountbatten on 31st March 1947 AD, suggested that the control of the Interim Government be handed completely to Md. Ali Jinnah who was the leader of the Muslim League so that these communal riots in India be stopped, but Congress leaders and Congress Working Committee didn’t support this proposal of Gandhi.
  • On partition, Gandhiji said, "If Congress wishes to accept partition it will be over my dead body". I will never be a supporter of partition till my last breath. If I were to choose I will never let Congress be ready for partition. Although Gandhi accepted the partition resolution at the All India Congress Committee (AICC) meeting held on 14-15 June 1947. Though he was fundamentally he opposed the idea of division of India. He urged Congress to accept the proposal to avoid further communal bloodshed.
  • J. B. Kripalani was the Congress President when All India Congress Committee in Delhi accepted the proposal of partition of India on 14-15 June, 1947 AD. This proposal was presented by Govind Ballabh Pant and Maulana Abul Kalam Azad seconded this proposal.
  • On November 1947, J.B. Kriplani resigned from Congress and Dr. Rajendra Prasad became the congress President. In Jaipur Session of Congress (1948 AD), Pattabhi Sitaramayya became the next Congress President. In the year 1950 AD, at Nasik session of Congress, Purushottam Das Tandon became the new Congress President. Nehru was President of Congress from 1951 to 1954 AD.
  • Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan (Frontier Gandhi) voted against the proposal for India’s partition at the meeting of All India Congress Working Committee on 14/15 June 1947 AD (mention of both dates are found).
  • Dr. Saifuddin Kitchlew upon the passing of this proposal said that today Nationalism surrendered to Communalism. He was President of the Congress Committee of Punjab Province and was against the partition. After Independence, he separated himself from Congress and later joined the Communist Party of India
  • On 14/15 August 1947 AD, at midnight Constituent Assembly assumed full powers for the governance of the country. Under the Act, the existing central Legislature ceased to exist and its place was taken by Constituent Assembly which, primarily a constitution making body, was to function as the Dominion Legislature as well. To avoid confusion, the two functions of the Assembly Constitution making and legislation were clearly separated and the Constituent Assembly (Legislative) commenced functioning from November 17, 1947. The meeting of Constituent Assembly was held at the midnight of 14 August.
  • On this occasion of Independence, Jawahar Lal Nehru gave a very influential speech in the Assembly. On 14th August 1947 AD, in the midnight 'Vande Mataram', 'Jan-Gan-Man' and 'Sare-Jahan-Se Achha' song was sung by Sucheta Kripalani. Jawaharlal Nehru was appointed as Prime Minister of India. Lord Mountbatten was the First Governor General of Independent India (1947- 48 AD) whereas C. Rajagopalachari was the First Indian Governor-General of Independent India (1948-50 AD).
  • C. Rajagopalachari during the years 1948-50 AD was the first and last Indian Governor-General of Independent India. He stayed on this post until 26th January, 1950 AD. He was the Chief Minister of Madras from year 1952 to 1954 AD. B.R. Ambedkar was the first Law Minister of free India. He worked as the Chairman of the Drafting Committee.
  • Indian national leaders wanted to make 26th January a memorable day (26 January 1930 Independence day celebration), that is why our constitution came into force on 26th January 1950 AD since it was prepared on 26 November, 1949 AD (many provisions like Article 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 60, 324 etc. have come into force from November 26, 1949). 26 January was declared as ‘Republic Day’.
  • R. Coupland said, "Indian nationalism in truth, was the child of the British Raj and the British authorities blessed its cradle". But he forgot that for him Indian nationalism was an undesirable child which was denied milk in the childhood, and after that, efforts were made to choke it till death.
  • On the unification of India by British rule K.M. Panikkar said, “The Greatest Achievement of British Rule is the Unity of India”.
